intro: Longer explanations of photonics, RF, SerDes, measurement, and power circuits, written for engineers who are new to them. Pick a category below.

notes.title: How a Mach–Zehnder modulator driver sets the limits of a radio-over-fiber link
notes.summary: Why Vπ, bias point, and the driver's output swing decide most of an analog photonic link's gain and dynamic range.

notes.title: RF essentials: noise figure, link budgets, and the numbers worth memorizing
notes.summary: dB arithmetic, power in 50 Ω, noise figure through one receiver chain, sensitivity, and the wavelength, antenna, cable, and propagation numbers every RF engineer should know.

notes.title: Microring resonators for circuit designers
notes.summary: Resonance, Q, and free spectral range, described with the LC-tank intuition analog engineers already have.

notes.title: Automatic tuning of silicon photonic ring filters
notes.summary: How a small control loop finds each ring's resonance and holds it there despite fabrication variation and temperature drift.

notes.title: SerDes design: circuits, standards, and where to start
notes.summary: An electrical I/O transceiver block by block, a map of today's standards from PCIe to UCIe, and a learning path of books, papers, and tools.

notes.title: Circuits for displays: pixel drivers, LEDs, switched-capacitor converters, and LDOs
notes.summary: How OLED and micro-LED pixels turn a stored voltage into light, how to model the LED, and how the panel's rails are made and kept quiet.

notes.title: Post-silicon measurement: characterizing chips circuit by circuit
notes.summary: Calibration and de-embedding, then how LNAs, mixers, PLLs, PAs, converters, links, and regulators are measured, including PA reliability and lifetime testing.
